title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart - Rondo Alla Turca
arrangement: Stephen's MIDI of the third movement of Piano Sonata K. 331 (a sequenced performance with repeats, tempo nuance and pedal), with this repo's dynamics pass: dynamics.mjs changes only note-on velocities. Second pass (2026-11-18), much stronger than the first: section levels with hairpins through each phrase (A-minor theme ~52-66, C-major episode forte ~96-102 then piano ~58-48, theme return crescendo 52-90, march building 96-114), melody over a doubled inner voice (-8) and the accompaniment (-16), accented march downbeats (+10) with lighter grace chords (-10). make-song.mjs bakes the pedal into the audio file's note lengths.

grid.note: 2/4, counted through the performance with every repeat played (223 bars). Bar 1 starts after the one-beat pickup (tick 256 at 256 ppq). The file's 1/4 time signatures are only the half bars where a section's end meets the next section's pickup, so downbeats stay on a steady 2/4 grid. Phrases are 8 bars: 1, 9, 17 ... 8k+1 through bar 192, then the coda (193-223).

sections.note: The A-minor theme opens on a one-beat pickup (B-A-G#-A). The march and the coda are the loud, Turkish-drum material; the coda has a piano subito at 205-211 before the last forte bars.

levelNote: The march into the coda: the loudest stretch any turn plays, so every piano's level is set where the limiter would bite first.
rights: Composition: public domain. Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791) published the Piano Sonata in A major, K. 331, with this Rondo Alla Turca in 1784. MIDI: from Stephen's own library (who sequenced the original performance is not recorded in the file), committed and published at his direction. Dynamics: this repo's pass (dynamics.mjs), velocities only. Never edit the original file; dynamics.mjs reads it and writes a separate copy.
